I've been working this land since I was a teenager helping my father. Forty years of wheat and maize in Quzhou — I know this soil, I know this weather, and I know what works. My 12 mu runs the full wheat-maize rotation: winter wheat goes in after the maize is off, summer maize goes straight back in after wheat harvest. Same ground, two crops a year, every year.

For **wheat**, I always do rotary tillage after the maize comes off in late September — gets the stubble worked in and the seedbed ready. I use the improved varieties, the ones the county extension station has been pushing for years — Jimai 22 has done well for me. I split my nitrogen: base application at planting, then topdress at jointing when the crop tells me it needs it. My well lets me irrigate four times — pre-sowing to settle moisture, winterizing water in December, jointing, and once at flowering. I do three pesticide passes: seed treatment, a spring herbicide sweep, and a fungicide at heading for rust and powdery mildew. I expect around 500 jin per mu — that's what I reliably pull when the season cooperates.

For **maize**, I go straight in with no-till right after wheat harvest in June. Time is short. I plant hybrid seed — Xianyu 335 has given me consistent results. July and August bring some rain, so my irrigation burden drops — I figure three waterings: at planting, at jointing, and at silking if it turns dry. I topdress nitrogen hard at the big leaf stage. Two pesticide rounds handles the aphids and stem borer. I target 550 jin per mu.
